all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] The fence toggle matches any 3-backtick line and ignores fence length, so a 4-backtick fence containing an inner ``` would toggle inFence off mid-block. Reachability is limited (no committed review log uses a 4-backtick fence; context packs are not parsed by Discover), so a latent gap rather than a live mis-parse.

[ADVISORY] The !inFence guard on the section-state switch and on the header boundary is not isolated by any fixture. A fenced non-mrvf level-2/3 heading closing the section (or opening it first) is untested, so removing the guard passes the suite.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Fenced-content skipping is asymmetric: section state and BlockingFindingIDs are guarded by !inFence, but the FindingIDs scrape is not, so ids quoted in a fenced block still land in FindingIDs. A fenced/quoted id the ledger holds as an open blocking-class row keeps the log a gate input after its declared blockers resolve — fail-closed (stays blocking), not fail-open.

[ADVISORY] The !inFence guard on the section-state switch and on the header boundary is not isolated by any fixture. A fenced non-mrvf level-2/3 heading closing the section (or opening it first) is untested, so removing the guard passes the suite.

[ADVISORY] The 'vouched == 0' guard in LogBlockersResolvedInLedger is not isolated — every case sets BlockingFindingCount >= 1, so the count tripwire fires first. The guard only bites when BlockingFindingCount==0 with an advisory-only blocking section; that input has no test, so deleting the guard passes CI.
